headline: Growth drugs outrun biosimilar erosion, profit up
summary_short: Amgen's Q3 revenue of $10.4B rose 8% y/y on volume growth, and GAAP EPS of $7.08 rose 19%. Free cash flow fell to $3.7B from $4.2B.
summary_long: Product sales grew 8% on volume; Repatha rose 37%, Evenity 39% and Uplizna 191%, while Prolia and Xgeva fell 45% and 47% as biosimilars launched. GAAP operating margin rose 9.9 points to 37.5% on lower amortization and manufacturing costs. R&D rose 11%. Free cash flow dropped on working-capital changes. No buybacks in the quarter; cash was $13.2B and debt $54.0B. FY2026 guidance: revenue $38.9–39.7B, non-GAAP EPS $22.90–23.70.
confidence_notes: Non-GAAP EPS and free cash flow are company-defined measures taken from the release. Revenue y/y of +8.5% is computed from reported dollar values; the release rounds to 8%.

drivers.explanation: Product sales grew 8% driven by volume growth; seventeen products posted double-digit growth, led by Repatha, Evenity, Tezspire and Imdelltra, partly offset by biosimilar erosion of Prolia and Xgeva.
EPS increase was driven by higher revenues, per the release.
GAAP cost of sales fell as a share of product sales on lower acquisition-related amortization and manufacturing costs, partly offset by higher profit share expense and mix; R&D rose 11%.
Driven primarily by higher revenues, partially offset by higher operating expenses.
Driven by changes in working capital; the prior-year quarter benefited from the timing of rebates and collections.
